4. Change `gn_apply_silu_res_t(..., const long* ptrs, float* out, int HW)`: `const float* __restrict__ res = (const float*)ptrs[0];` (same slot 0 as the transpose, so residual and transpose always read the same buffer). Keep gn_stats_partial and gn_apply_silu signatures unchanged.
5. Change `gn_finalize(..., const long* ptrs, int gSlot, int bSlot, ...)`: `const float* gamma=(const float*)ptrs[gSlot]; const float* beta=(const float*)ptrs[bSlot];` (slots 2/3 for stage1, 5/6 for stage2).
6. Add kernel `w_nchw_to_nhwc(const long* ptrs, int slot, float* dst)` for the fixed (256,256,3,3) weight: grid=(256), block=256; for o=blockIdx.x, each thread t<256 loops kh,kw in 0..2 (`#pragma unroll`) writing `dst[((o*3+kh)*3+kw)*256 + t] = src[((o*256+t)*3+kh)*3+kw]`, src=(const float*)ptrs[slot]. This replaces `conv1_weight.contiguous(ChannelsLast)` (an aten op, not a carried optimisation) so the weight source pointer is no longer baked into the graph; the destination is a graph-private `at::empty({256,256,3,3}, ChannelsLast)`.
7. New host entry `fused_block_ptr(torch::Tensor ptrs_dev, int64_t N, int64_t H, int64_t W, double eps)`: identical body to `fused_block` except it takes no data tensors — it allocates w1_cl/w2_cl and runs w_nchw_to_nhwc, then the same at::conv2d NHWC TF32 calls, the same 3 GroupNorm kernels per stage, passing `(const long*)ptrs_dev.data_ptr<int64_t>()` where needed.
8. Python: in `__init__` create `self._ph = torch.empty(7, dtype=torch.int64, pin_memory=True)`, `self._pd = torch.empty(7, dtype=torch.int64, device='cuda')`, `self._graphs = {}`, `self._ws = torch.cuda.Stream()`.
9. forward guard unchanged (cuda, fp32, dim4, C==256) plus `x.is_contiguous()`; otherwise the existing eager fallback.
10. Every call: write the 7 `t.data_ptr()` values into `self._ph`, then `self._pd.copy_(self._ph, non_blocking=True)` on the current stream (56 bytes). No other copies.
11. Cache key `(tuple(x.shape), float(eps), x.device.index)`. On miss: on `self._ws` (after wait_stream) call `fused_block_ptr` 3× to force cuDNN autotune/workspace, sync, then `g=torch.cuda.CUDAGraph(); with torch.cuda.graph(g): out = fused_block_ptr(self._pd, N,H,W,eps)`; store `(g,out)`. Wrap in try/except; on failure store None and permanently call `fused_block_ptr` eagerly for that key.
12. Steady state: pointer copy, `g.replay()`, `return out` (static graph-private output). Never re-capture for a seen key, never allocate or synchronize on the replay path.
strategy.evidence: History classification (b): Attempt #1's predicted end-to-end drop did NOT materialise — it regressed uniformly (-5.0/-4.6/-4.9/-4.5% per shape) while all kernel metrics were unchanged (nchw dram 77.41 vs 78.10, res_t 84.82 vs 84.75). The defect is identifiable arithmetically: the mandatory `sx.copy_(x)` moves 2x67.1MB (8*256*64*128*4) per mid-shape forward, ~134MB of extra DRAM traffic; at the measured 1.72e12 B/s of gn_apply_silu_res_t that is ~78us against a 1043us forward, i.e. the copy alone exceeds the entire measured 5.0% regression — the graph saved something, the copy ate it. Concrete delta vs Attempt #1: no bulk static-input copy at all; a 56-byte pointer table plus in-kernel pointer dereference replaces it, and the two conv-weight channels-last conversions move from aten (24 launches, 156us) into a graph-internal kernel. Current-profile numbers confirm there is no intra-kernel headroom to chase instead: gpu__dram_throughput = 84.75% (res_t), 79.95% (gn_stats_partial), 78.1% (transpose), and the section text for gn_apply_silu_res_t states 'This workload is utilizing greater than 80.0% of the available compute or memory performance of this device'. Ruled out as secondary: occupancy/warp supply — achieved occupancy 91.82% on the transpose and 82.32% on gn_apply_silu, 32 regs/thread, smsp__sass_branch_targets_threads_divergent = 0.0, so no divergence or occupancy limit. Also ruled out: the UncoalescedSharedAccess finding on gn_apply_silu_res_t (42% excessive wavefronts) — that kernel is 8.0% of forward GPU time and already at 84.75% of DRAM peak, capping any fix near 1%. This plan composes with the carried coalesced_tile_transpose (kernel unchanged, only its input pointer source changes) and keeps the autotuned sm90_xmma nhwc TF32 conv engines.
strategy.expected_metric_change: end_to_end forward time ↓ on all four shapes vs base 1.6216 (largest relative gain on 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 where dispatch dominates); host-visible launches per forward ↓ from ~13 kernels + 24 aten weight-conversion launches to 1 graph replay + 1 56-byte H2D; extra DRAM bytes per forward ↓ from +134MB (Attempt #1) to +56 bytes. Anti-regression: (a) per-kernel gpu__dram_throughput must stay at 78.1/79.95/84.75% and launch__registers_per_thread at 32/36 with Local Memory Spilling Requests = 0 — any drop means the pointer dereference hurt the inner loops; (b) `nchw_to_nhwc_tiled` must still appear in the timeline at ~71us on the mid shape (its disappearance would mean the carried coalesced_tile_transpose was lost); (c) the sm90_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm ...nhwckrsc_nhwc TF32 engines must still be selected and no nchwToNhwc/nhwcToNchw helper kernel may appear — that would mean w_nchw_to_nhwc wrote the wrong weight layout; (d) capture must happen once per shape key, never per iteration; (e) if, with the bulk copies removed, all four shapes STILL regress, the launch-overhead model is falsified (case (a)) and this direction must be abandoned rather than retried.
